lesson.title: Decision patterns and human review
lesson.summary: Distinguish pattern detection with proper review from unreviewed alteration of a completed assessment.

prerequisites.reason: The pattern-review test explicitly limits replacement or influence of a prior human assessment.

blocks: The **pattern-review condition** concerns detecting decision-making patterns or deviations. It is qualified by the requirement that the system is not meant to replace or influence a previously completed human assessment without proper human review.
Read the entire condition together. 'Pattern detector' alone is not sufficient, and 'human review' needs a real process rather than a ceremonial button.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 6(3)(c), paragraph 3 gateway and profiling rule

blocks: Fictional Northbridge: a tool flags a deviation across completed assessments; a competent reviewer examines the underlying work before any revision. Record the flag, access to evidence and what the reviewer can actually change.
This illustrates facts relevant to the condition. It does not by itself establish the no-significant-risk gateway or eliminate the profiling check.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 6(3)(c), paragraph 3 gateway and profiling rule

blocks: Changed case: each flag automatically replaces the prior assessment without proper review. That undermines the stated condition.

Changed case: the reviewer sees only the flag and routinely approves it without examining the earlier basis. Evidence of actual review is needed before calling it proper. A workflow diagram alone cannot establish how review functions.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 6(3)(c), paragraph 3 gateway and profiling rule

blocks: Keep the completed assessment, pattern function, review arrangements and consequences in the record. Assess whether output materially influences decisions and whether the person can challenge errors.
The derogation is not a general authorisation for replacing decisions after a token human step. If facts do not establish the condition or gateway, do not claim the exception.
